items.titleZh: 维斯塔潘2027过渡首步：哈特首次全程执掌比赛工程师
items.summaryZh: 红牛开始让汤姆·哈特在比赛中承担更多比赛工程师职责，为兰比亚塞最迟2028年转投迈凯伦做准备；哈特在美国大奖赛首次全程负责维斯塔潘的比赛工程师工作，但无线电故障和策略问题让这个周末并不顺利。

media.altZh: 维斯塔潘2027过渡首步：哈特首次全程执掌比赛工程师 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: How first step in Verstappen's big F1 2027 transition really went
items.summaryEn: Red Bull has begun giving Tom Hart more race engineer responsibilities as it prepares for Gianpiero Lambiase's move to McLaren by 2028 at the latest, and Hart took charge of Verstappen for an entire weekend for the first time at the United States Grand Prix, a race complicated by radio problems and strategy frustration.
detailZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘告别长期F1比赛工程师詹皮耶罗·兰比亚塞的第一步并不顺利，原因是一场混乱的美国大奖赛。
然而，起步表现平平、被形容为“灾难”的无线电通讯问题，以及对策略的不满，都与他的未来工程师汤姆·哈特首次在他身边工作无关。
作为红牛为兰比亚塞最迟2028年转投迈凯伦而逐步让其退出的准备工作的一部分，车队已开始把更多职责交给他的接替者哈特。
哈特自夏休期以来已在几节练习中代班，在奥斯汀则首次整个周末上岗，兰比亚塞在幕后观察。
这不是一个轻松的周末，尤其是因为车队至今仍对无线电问题感到困惑，但考虑到这是哈特与维斯塔潘首次合作参赛，红牛对事情进展感到乐观。
车队领队洛朗·梅基斯表示：“我认为他（哈特）做得非常出色，你看到我微笑是因为我当然记得第一次担任比赛工程师是什么感觉——而他选择了一场相当复杂的比赛来完成这个首秀。”
红牛知道车手与工程师之间的强大默契无法一夜之间建立，所以即使哈特与维斯塔潘彼此非常了解，他们也需要时间才能达到维斯塔潘与兰比亚塞之间那种默契水平。
梅基斯表示，他在这个周末的印象是，这种默契已经尽可能地稳定下来了。
梅基斯在谈到哈特时表示：“第一次参加排位赛、第一场正赛，他很好地承接了身后工程团队为维斯塔潘所做的工作。”
“这场比赛是一场复杂的比赛，我们可能对第三名有些沮丧，但这是好消息。不过我真的认为他做得非常出色，而且他在幕后也得到了兰比亚塞的很好支持。”
“我确信你无法在短时间内重建一段关系，但我完全相信我们会看到他逐步加强并与维斯塔潘建立那种关系。”
红牛计划在本赛季剩余时间里继续发展这段关系，哈特和兰比亚塞将在余下的比赛中轮流担任该角色。
从更长远来看，尽管哈特将从2027年初开始全面接手，但兰比亚塞将继续承担多少指导角色尚不清楚。这在很大程度上取决于他还会在红牛参与多久。
兰比亚塞何时加入迈凯伦担任其新任首席竞赛官，目前尚未商定日期，而他在红牛的合同要到明年年底才到期。
红牛并不急于提前放他走，而迈凯伦则希望尽可能早地得到他——理想情况下是在2027年的某个时候。
在上个月于马德里举行的西班牙大奖赛上，迈凯伦首席执行官扎克·布朗在围场与兰比亚塞举行了一次毫不掩饰的公开会面，以在与红牛继续讨论的同时引起人们对这一事的关注。
红牛的首要任务是尽可能长时间地留住兰比亚塞，以确保向新架构平稳过渡，这一新架构还包括阿斯顿·马丁的汤姆·麦卡洛的到来，他将担任新的赛事主管。
尽管哈特已在新岗位上开始熟悉工作，但麦卡洛要到明年一月才开始在米尔顿凯恩斯工作——这意味着如果兰比亚塞要协助那里的交接，他至少得留任到明年年初。
detailEn: Max Verstappen's first step towards life away from long-serving Formula 1 race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase was not straightforward, thanks to a messy United States Grand Prix.

A middling start, radio communication problems that were labelled a "disaster", and annoyance over the strategy had, however, nothing to do with his future engineer Tom Hart being at his side for the first time.
As part of Red Bull's preparations to phase Lambiase out ahead of his switch to McLaren, by 2028 at the latest, the team has begun handing his replacement Hart more responsibilities.
Hart had already filled in during a few practice sessions since the summer break and at Austin he stepped up for the entire weekend, with Lambiase keeping a watching brief in the background.

It was not an easy weekend, especially because of the radio problems that the team remains baffled by, but Red Bull was upbeat about how things went considering it was Hart and Verstappen's first race together.

Team principal Laurent Mekies said: "I think he [Hart] did an excellent job, and you see me smiling because I certainly remember what it is to be on your first race as a race engineer - and he picked a fairly complicated race to do that."

Red Bull knows that a strong dynamic between driver and engineer cannot be built overnight, so even though Hart and Verstappen know each other very well it is going to take time for them to reach the level of understanding that Verstappen has enjoyed with Lambiase.
Mekies said that his impression over the weekend was that the dynamic had bedded down as well as could be expected.
"First qualifying, first race, he has managed to channel very well the work of the engineering teams behind him, to Max," said Mekies of Hart.

"The race was a complicated race, and we are probably a bit frustrated with the P3, which is good news. But I really think he did an excellent job, and he was very well supported by GP [Lambiase] as well in the background.
"I'm sure you cannot recreate a relationship in no time, but I have every confidence that we are going to see him ramping up and building that relationship with Max."
Red Bull plans to continue evolving that relationship throughout the rest of this season, with Hart and Lambiase set to alternate the role over the remaining races.

Longer term, while Hart is set to take over fully from the beginning of 2027, it is not clear how much of a mentoring role Lambiase will continue to have. That will very much depend on how long he remains involved at Red Bull.
No date has yet been agreed for when Lambiase will join McLaren as its new chief racing officer, and his contract at Red Bull does not run out until the end of next year.
Red Bull is not eager to let him go early, while McLaren wants to get hold of him as early as possible - ideally at some point in 2027.
At the Spanish GP in Madrid last month, McLaren CEO Zak Brown held a brazen public meeting with Lambiase in the paddock to help draw attention to the matter as discussions continue with Red Bull.

The priority for Red Bull is to hold on to Lambiase for as long as it needs to ensure that there is a smooth transition to a new structure, which also includes the arrival of Aston Martin's Tom McCullough as its new head of racing.

And while Hart has started to get his feet under the desk in his new role, McCullough does not begin work at Milton Keynes until January - which means Lambiase will have to remain on board at least until the early part of next year if he is to assist in the handover there.
keyPointsZh: 哈特自夏休期以来已在几节练习中代班，在奥斯汀则首次整个周末担任比赛工程师，兰比亚塞在幕后观察。
车队领队梅基斯称哈特做得非常出色，并指出他首场就赶上了一场相当复杂的比赛。
keyPointsEn: Hart had already filled in during a few practice sessions since the summer break, and at Austin he stepped up for the entire weekend while Lambiase kept a watching brief in the background.
Team principal Mekies said Hart did an excellent job and noted that he picked a fairly complicated race for his first one.

items.titleZh: 阿斯顿·马丁与红牛澄清引擎合作传闻
items.summaryZh: 在美国大奖赛后的媒体环节中，阿斯顿·马丁与红牛代表被问及一个与比赛无关的引擎合作话题。阿斯顿·马丁坚称在艰难开局后仍全力投入本田，红牛动力总成则表示目前既无雄心也无产能为红牛体系外的客户车队供应该引擎。

media.altZh: 阿斯顿·马丁与红牛澄清引擎合作传闻 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Why Aston Martin and Red Bull were asked about an unlikely F1 engine partnership
items.summaryEn: During the post-race media sessions at the United States Grand Prix, representatives of Aston Martin and Red Bull were asked about an engine partnership topic unrelated to the race. Aston Martin insisted it remains fully committed to Honda after a difficult start, while Red Bull Powertrains said it currently has neither the ambition nor the capacity to supply a customer team from outside the Red Bull organisation.
detailZh: 阿斯顿·马丁与红牛为何被问及一个看似不太可能的F1引擎合作
阿斯顿·马丁坚称在艰难开局后仍全力投入本田，而红牛动力总成表示目前既无雄心也无产能为红牛体系外的客户车队供应引擎
费尔南多·阿隆索，阿斯顿·马丁车队，伊萨克·哈贾尔，红牛车队
周日奥斯汀最引人注目的时刻之一并非发生在赛道上，而是在美国大奖赛后的F1围场里。在常规的赛后媒体环节中，阿斯顿·马丁与红牛的代表都被问及一个与美洲赛道比赛几乎无关的话题——事实上恰恰相反。
阿斯顿·马丁的首席赛道官迈克·克拉克和红牛车队领队洛朗·梅基斯都被问及，他们能否排除这两个品牌未来潜在合作的可能性。这似乎相当离奇，当这个问题在他们的媒体采访环节中随机出现时，两人理所当然地显得很惊讶，这就是为什么这件事需要一些背景说明。
这一切都要追溯到一篇BBC的文章以及对其某种不幸的解读。在F1记者安德鲁·本森的常规问答专栏中，有人问他，鉴于红牛福特动力单元在第一个赛季似乎极具竞争力，客户车队是否可能对它感兴趣。
答案非常明确地表明，目前没有F1车队在寻找动力单元，随后正确地强调了一个围场内广为人知的事实：今年早些时候，当F1新时代伊始本田在动力单元方面的落后程度变得显而易见时，阿斯顿·马丁尤其是车队老板劳伦斯·斯特罗尔感到震惊。
这理所当然地导致了一些最初的疑虑和考量，尽管最终决定继续全力投入本田——BBC的文章也正确地强调了这一点。唯一留下些许余地的推测性因素是，如果本田未能在比如2027年或2028年取得预期的进步，那些疑虑可能会重新浮现。
正如F1和当今媒体环境中经常发生的那样，据多位内部人士称，这个故事随后自行发酵，成为了一个本不该如此受关注的更大话题。这是一个自我实现的预言：只要F1围场里有足够多的人被问及某事，无论对错，它都会自动成为一个话题，进而产生报道。这是一种滚雪球效应，因此对此类故事进行客观审视至关重要。
阿斯顿·马丁的视角：放弃潜在的工作协议将极其草率
克拉克和梅基斯在周日晚上都被问及，他们能否否认阿斯顿·马丁与红牛动力总成之间正在进行谈判，这个问题的言外之意自然远远超出了BBC原文章中的任何暗示。克拉克迅速重申了阿斯顿·马丁对本田的长期承诺。
本田赛车公司赛道总经理兼首席工程师折原慎太郎
“我只能说，我们有一个长期合作伙伴，那就是本田，顺便说一句，本周末它已经完成了第500场比赛。而且我认为，当我们一起赢得第一场比赛时，我们也会在一起。”阿斯顿·马丁的代表说道。
需要指出的是，目前的合作伙伴关系和工作协议在理论上提供了巨大的潜力。是的，本田确实还远未达到理想水平，但这家日本制造商此前已经证明，它能够扭转困难局面——想想它和迈凯伦的糟糕开局，最终却与红牛一起赢得了多个世界冠军。
这与阿德里安·纽维在奥斯汀国际汽联新闻发布会上的评论相呼应。当被问及在红牛困难时期所谓的动力问题时，他含蓄地指出了当时车队的引擎合作伙伴雷诺与目前本田关系之间的关键区别。
“作为底盘设计师，如果动力单元制造商有一个糟糕的年份，那就会发生，你接受它。但如果动力单元制造商有一个糟糕的年份，而且似乎没有任何意图去解决问题，那就是完全不同的事情了，到那个时候情况就相当黯淡了。”
“不幸的是，这就是我们在2014年面临的情况。而事实证明，直到我们在2019年改用本田之前，那个供应商带来的情况并没有真正改变。所以，你可以想象我当时有多痛苦和沮丧。”
然而，与本田合作时，情况就大不相同了。这家日本制造商敏锐地意识到当前的短板，并正全力以赴扭转局面，纽维也强调了这一点。
“在本田，现在有大量的精力和项目正在推进，这些或许还处于开发的早期阶段，但我们从中看到了很大的希望。”
这既说明了本田的决心，也说明了从更长远来看仍然存在的潜力。阿斯顿·马丁特意选择了厂商合作，因为这标志着车队发展演变的下一个阶段。
与作为客户车队相比，这不仅提供了更好的机会来塑造合作伙伴关系，还带来了将动力单元更有效地整合到底盘并相互帮助的潜在好处——这是纽维和本田都认定的2027年的关键优先事项。两个品牌仍然完全认识到这一潜力，这使得放弃厂商合作协议极不可能，而且，这是一种极其短视的做法——一种膝跳反应。
红牛的视角：尚未准备好供应客户车队
所有这些都解释了为什么从阿斯顿·马丁的角度来看，继续沿着当前道路前进、给予时间并最终收获这一厂商合作伙伴关系的回报是完全合理的。
然后，当然，还有红牛方面的说法。是的，其与福特合作的动力总成项目起步比许多人想象的要好得多，但据梅基斯称，这并不自动意味着公司已准备好迈出供应客户车队的一步。
“瞧，我们的引擎性能引来了许多不必要的正面关注，这当然也引起了众多车队的注意，”梅基斯笑着说道，他指的是国际汽联的ADUO排名以及未获得研发令牌一事。
“我们有没有和任何人认真谈过为另一支车队供应引擎？没有，我们觉得自己还没准备好。这事未来五年就板上钉钉了吗？没有，因为我不知道未来五年会发生什么。
“但对我们来说，肯定有足够的工作要做，去改进动力单元、改进它在赛车上的集成，并在考虑为小红牛之外再供应一支车队之前，先达到最佳竞争对手的水平。所以未来一年左右不会有任何变化。”
劳伦特·梅基斯，红牛车队领队
制造商向客户车队提供引擎的主要原因之一是收集更多数据，这有利于研发。这也是可能拖累本田的因素之一，因为它只供应一支车队，而且由于所有可靠性问题，在冬季测试和赛季初的比赛中收集到的数据非常少。
然而，对红牛来说，这并非立即接手客户车队的动机，因为它已经有一支客户车队，即其姊妹车队 小红牛。这家位于米尔顿凯恩斯的制造商已经供应两支车队，因此有四辆车可以收集数据。
所有这些意味着，从阿斯顿·马丁和红牛双方的角度来看，这样的合作目前显然不是一个显而易见的选择。关键是要从这个角度看待最近的猜测——换句话说，放在正确的背景下。可以理解，很多事情将取决于本田未来几年的发展，但就目前而言，这又是一个经常成为 F1 围场和当今媒体格局特征的例子：小题大做。
detailEn: Why Aston Martin and Red Bull were asked about an unlikely F1 engine partnership

Aston Martin insists it remains fully committed to Honda after a difficult start, while Red Bull Powertrains says it currently has neither the ambition nor the capacity to supply a customer team from outside the Red Bull organisation
Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

One of the most remarkable moments on Sunday in Austin did not take place on the track itself, but rather in the Formula 1 paddock after the US Grand Prix. During the usual post-race media sessions, both Aston Martin and Red Bull’s representatives were asked about a subject that had very little to do with the race at the Circuit of the Americas – quite the opposite, in fact.

Both Aston Martin's chief trackside officer Mike Krack and Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies were asked whether they could rule out a potential partnership between the two brands in the future. It seems rather extraordinary, and both men understandably looked surprised when that question randomly came up during their media rounds, which is why the matter requires some context.

It all goes back to a BBC article and a somewhat unfortunate interpretation of it. In the regular Q&A column of F1 correspondent Andrew Benson, he was asked whether customer teams might be interested in the Red Bull Ford power unit, given that it appears to be more than competitive in its first year.

The answer made it abundantly clear that no F1 team is currently looking for a power unit and then rightly highlighted something that is widely known in the paddock: the shock at Aston Martin, particularly for team owner Lawrence Stroll, when it became apparent earlier this year just how far behind Honda was on the power unit side at the start of F1’s new era.

That understandably led to some initial doubts and considerations, although the decision was made to remain fully committed to Honda – something the BBC article also correctly emphasised. The only speculative element that left the door slightly open was the possibility that those doubts could resurface if Honda fails to make the expected step forward in, let’s say, 2027 or 2028.

As so often happens in F1 and today's media landscape, the story subsequently took on a life of its own and became a bigger talking point than it should have been, according to several insiders. It is a self-fulfilling prophecy: something automatically becomes a topic, rightly or wrongly, if enough people in the F1 paddock are asked about it, which in turn generates coverage. It is a snowball effect, making it crucial to put such stories into perspective.
The Aston Martin perspective: Abandoning works deal potential would be extremely premature

Both Krack and Mekies were asked on Sunday evening whether they could deny that talks were taking place between Aston Martin and Red Bull Powertrains, with the implication of that question naturally going considerably further than anything suggested in the original BBC article. Krack was quick to reaffirm Aston Martin's long-term commitment to Honda.
Shintaro Orihara, Honda Racing Corporation Trackside General Manager and Chief Engineer

“I can only say we have a long-term partner, which is Honda, that by the way has done its 500th race this weekend. And I think we will be together also when we win our first race together”, the Aston Martin representative said.

It is important to point out that the current partnership and works deal offer enormous potential in theory. Yes, it is true that Honda is nowhere near the desired level yet, but the Japanese manufacturer has previously demonstrated that it can turn a difficult situation around – just think of its false start with McLaren, which eventually led to multiple world titles with Red Bull.

This ties in with Adrian Newey's comments during the FIA press conference in Austin. When asked about alleged motivation problems during the difficult years at Red Bull, he implicitly pointed to a crucial difference between the team's engine partner at the time, Renault, and its current relationship with Honda.

“As a chassis designer, if the PU manufacturer has a bad year, that happens, and you accept it. But if the PU manufacturer has a bad year and doesn’t appear to have any intention of trying to address the problem, that’s altogether a different matter, and that’s quite bleak at that point.

“That’s the situation that unfortunately we faced in 2014. And as it turned out, that situation didn’t really change with that supplier until we changed to Honda in 2019. So, you can imagine my pain and frustration at that time.”

With Honda, however, the situation is very different. The Japanese manufacturer is acutely aware of the current shortcomings and is pulling out all the stops to turn the situation around, something Newey also highlighted.
“At Honda, there’s a lot of energy and projects on the way now that perhaps are in their early stages of development, but we see a lot of promise from those.”

That says something about Honda's determination, but also about the potential that still exists in the longer term. Aston Martin deliberately opted for a works deal, as it marks the next step in the team's evolution.

Not only does it offer a much better opportunity to shape the partnership than would be possible as a customer team, it also brings the potential benefits of integrating the power unit more effectively into the chassis and helping each other – something both Newey and Honda have identified as a crucial priority for 2027. Both brands still fully recognise that potential, which makes abandoning a works deal highly unlikely and, moreover, an extremely short-term approach – something of a knee-jerk reaction.
The Red Bull perspective: Not yet ready to supply a customer team
All of this explains why, from Aston Martin's perspective, it would make perfect sense to continue down the current path, give it time and eventually reap the rewards of this works partnership.

And then, of course, there is Red Bull's side of the story. Yes, its own powertrains project in collaboration with Ford has made a considerably better start than many thought possible, but according to Mekies, that does not automatically mean the company is ready to take the step towards supplying customer teams.

“Look, we got a lot of unwanted, positive publicity about the performance of our engine and that certainly came with attention from a lot of teams”, Mekies smiled, referring to the FIA’s ADUO ranking and not receiving a development token.

“Are we having any serious conversations with anyone to supply another team? No, we don't feel we are ready for that. Is it set in stone for the next five years? No, because I don't know what's going to happen in the next five years.

“But for sure for us, there is enough work on our side to improve the power unit, to improve its integrations in the car, and to get at the level of the best competitors before we can consider being able to supply one more team on top of Racing Bulls. So nothing will change in the next year or so.”
Laurent Mekies, Red Bull Racing Team Principal

One of the main reasons for a manufacturer to supply engines to a customer team is to gather more data, which can benefit development. It is one of the factors that may be hampering Honda, given that it supplies just one team and was able to collect very little data during winter testing and the opening races because of all the reliability problems.

For Red Bull, however, that is not an immediate incentive to take on a customer team, as it already has one in the form of its sister team Racing Bulls. The Milton Keynes-based manufacturer already supplies two teams and therefore has four cars from which to gather data.

All of this means that, from both Aston Martin's and Red Bull's perspectives, such a partnership is certainly not an obvious option at present. It is crucial to view the recent speculation in that light – in other words, in the right context. It is understandable that much will depend on Honda's development over the coming years, but for now, this is another example of something that frequently characterises the F1 paddock and today's media landscape: a storm in a teacup.

items.titleZh: 国际汽联与AWS合作，AI将参与未来F1赛车设计
items.summaryZh: 国际汽联与亚马逊云科技（AWS）达成新合作，更强大的人工智能工具将在F1空气动力学规则制定中发挥更大作用。AWS将成为国际汽联官方人工智能、云计算、机器学习和云基础设施合作伙伴。
items.originalTitle: AI will help design future F1 cars in new FIA/AWS deal
items.summaryEn: The FIA has entered a new partnership with Amazon Web Services under which more powerful AI tools will play a bigger role in developing Formula 1's aerodynamic regulations. AWS will become the FIA's official artificial intelligence, cloud computing, machine learning and cloud infrastructure partner.
detailZh: 作为国际汽联与亚马逊云科技（AWS）新合作的一部分，更强大的人工智能工具将在F1空气动力学规则的制定中发挥更大作用。
AWS将成为国际汽联官方的人工智能、云计算、机器学习和云基础设施合作伙伴，其职责范围包括以更好的空气动力学模拟来塑造未来规则、协助改进国际汽联在全球的许可系统，以及更深入地融入国际汽联的内部运作方式。
与国际汽联合作开展计算流体力学（CFD）测试，旨在借助更新的硬件实现更快、更高保真度的模拟，并在模拟之上叠加人工智能加速手段，再由人工智能核查规则手册本身。
不过，生成式人工智能暂不会用于提出设计思路，因为当前的优先事项是用这些工具加速并支持人类工作。
在CFD工作的核心使用AWS，将其纳入国际汽联自己的虚拟风洞，并支持概念车的创建，这些概念车可以检查诸如跟随另一辆车时损失多少下压力，以及规则是否产生国际汽联想要的比赛。
虚拟过程涉及将汽车零件的3D数字图纸组装成模型，将汽车周围的空气分成数百万个微小单元，以便逐单元求解方程，然后后处理将原始数字转化为压力图、流动可视化和国际汽联可以分析的力。
国际汽联F1副技术总监多米尼克·哈洛解释说：“AWS硬件构建了那个简报，所以这是一个传统的CFD过程，使用OpenFOAM[一个开源软件包]和各种后处理工具运行。
“然后除此之外，CFD数据查看和操作的增强可能来自人工智能。
“因此，我们可能会考虑使用一些基于我们计算流体动力学（CFD）数据训练出的代理方法，来简化模拟过程，从而以更少的计算时间、更少的工程时间、更少的能源消耗和更少的资金，从整个流程中获得更高的生产力。”
尽管当前规则集才进入第一年，但针对可能于2030年推出的全新赛车和引擎的工作已经在进行中。
哈洛认为，风洞、计算流体动力学（CFD）和人工智能工作将相互关联，以制定这些规则，要么填补赛道数据的空白，要么单纯增强虚拟开发工作量。
完整的计算流体动力学（CFD）运行可能需要数小时，而哈洛提到的代理模型则是一种基于数百个过往CFD结果训练的人工智能，它学习形状与结果之间的关系，然后在几秒或几分钟内预测新形状的结果，而无需求解物理方程。
对国际汽联而言，这意味着要在相同时间内测试更多规则草案的变体——例如翼片形状和底板几何结构——但好处也延伸到了非空气动力学方面，国际汽联的性能部门正在研究电子设备和发动机法规。
“所以在性能方面，他们拥有计算机视觉[图像/视频分析]等工具，这些工具使我们能够将收集到的许多指标仪表化展示，其中一些用于安全，一些用于能量管理，一些用于合法性检查等等，”哈洛说。
“因此，我们收到的许多数据，可以利用人工智能更快地处理，用于趋势监测、发现模式，基本上，这是它擅长的事情之一。
“同样，对于动力单元，他们在动力单元[PU]小组中使用这类工具进行异常检测，因此神经网络可以表示你想要的任何连续函数。
如果你给它足够的神经元，你就能绘制出最复杂的波浪线，然后将这些波浪线与赛道上采集到的数据进行比较，从而看出某人的油压何时下降或其他情况。
神经网络是基本的人工智能结构，其规模足以对任何模式进行建模——而异常检测的工作原理是学习正常轨迹的样子，然后标记任何偏离该轨迹的情况。
这对于为国际汽联的分析提供信息更有用，因为人工智能工具本质上擅长根据对输入数据的查询来预测不同事件的结果。
构建能够边运行边学习的模型，还将使这一过程从一次性的规则制定转变为持续循环，因为这些工具会学习任何新法规在实际运行中的运作方式并不断演进。
当规则发生重大变化、以往数据无法准确反映新赛车时，这一点很有用；但需要注意的是，神经网络可能是所谓的黑箱，其内部决策过程对人类来说难以或无法追溯，因此国际汽联需要能够理解其工具为何标记了某些问题。
而且由于F1赛车如此复杂，目前人工智能工具在创造全新事物方面能力较弱，不过“提示工程”这一概念有可能在更远的将来成为现实。
“基于对这些[2026年]赛车的认识，已经开始为未来赛车研究新的空气动力学概念，”哈洛说。“还有一些我们可以尝试和调查的不同想法。
“我想人工智能的生成部分是我们未来可以想象的，但目前它是由人驱动、由工程师驱动的。”
“对你的赛车进行提示词工程，这显然全都关乎训练和模型的演进，而且要做这些事情肯定需要大量算力和大量资金。”
“我相信这一定会实现。”
国际汽联应当能够通过其与AWS的合作关系获益的一个领域，就是获取最新的图形处理器硬件。
计算流体动力学传统上在CPU上运行，但相关软件现在正被改写为在GPU上运行，速度往往快上数倍，并且能够同时处理海量简单计算，这既适合人工智能，也适合计算流体动力学。更好的硬件意味着更快、更准确的结果。
哈洛举了2022年地效时代初期让多支车队和国际汽联措手不及的海豚跳效应为例，说明这类现象有可能从中受益。
“因此，不必只运行一轮稳态计算流体力学模拟，你可以在非稳态条件下运行对时间敏感的模拟，”哈洛说。
“也许对于像海豚跳这样的现象，可以在它成为问题之前，或在全尺寸上看到它之前，获得更多理解。”
人工智能可能融入国际汽联流程的另一个领域，是使用更贴合用途的大语言模型，来支持车队对合法性问题的咨询以及对法规的压力测试。
这意味着要打造一个比 ChatGPT 或 Claude 类人工智能更私密、更安全的版本，以圈护知识产权，使机密材料留在国际汽联内部，但又能用来核查如此庞大、复杂的规则手册及其相互关联的条款。
用途之广还包括协助管理安全、能源管理和赛道合法性检查的仪表板，并支持日内瓦增强型远程运营中心，该中心在赛事期间远程支持赛事控制。
这可能包括协助处理赛道限制，因为当前的自动化系统会抛出数百起事件，需要人工核查，而人工智能可以提供一份按优先级排序的清单，或在做出判断前提示进行一系列检查，这样仍由人类做决定，但能更快、更一致地完成。
detailEn: More powerful AI tools will play a bigger part in the development of Formula 1's aerodynamic rules as part of a new partnership between the FIA and Amazon Web Services.

AWS will be the FIA's official artificial intelligence, cloud computing, machine learning and cloud infrastructure partner with the scope to shape future regulations with better aero simulations, assist with improvements to the FIA's licensing systems globally, and be more integrated in how the FIA operates internally.

Running CFD testing with AWS is intended to unlock faster, higher-fidelity simulation on newer hardware, with AI shortcuts layered on top of that simulation and then AI checking of the rulebook itself.
Generative AI will not be used to prompt design ideas yet, though, as the priority is to use the tools to accelerate and support human work.

Using AWS at the core of the CFD work brings it into the FIA's own virtual windtunnel and supports the creation of concept cars that can check things such as how much downforce is lost when following another car and whether the rules produce the racing the FIA wants.

The virtual process involved 3D digital drawings of car parts that are assembled into models, with the air around the car divided into millions of tiny cells so equations can be solved cell by cell, then post-processing turns raw numbers into pressure maps, flow visualisations and forces the FIA can analyse.

FIA deputy technical director for F1 Dominic Harlow explained: "AWS hardware builds that brief, so that's a traditional CFD process run using OpenFOAM [an open-source software package] and various post-processing tools.
"Then alongside that, the enhancements to CFD data viewing and manipulation could come from AI.

"So we might look at using some surrogate approaches trained off our CFD data to shortcut the simulations, to get more productivity out of the whole process for less compute time, less engineering time, less energy consumption and less money."
Though the current ruleset is only in its first year, work is already under way for what could be a 2030 introduction for brand new cars and engines.
Harlow believes windtunnel, CFD and AI work will be cross-correlated to develop these rules, either to fill in the gaps in track data or simply to enhance the virtual development workload.

A full CFD run can take hours whereas a surrogate model as Harlow mentions would be an AI trained on hundreds of past CFD results, which learns the relationship between shape and outcome, then predicts the result for a new shape in seconds or minutes without solving the physics.

For the FIA that means testing many more variations of a draft rule - such as wing shapes and floor geometries - in the same time but the benefits extend to the non-aero side with the FIA's performance department looking at electronics and engine regulations.

"So in performance, they've got tools like computer vision [image/video analysis], tools that enable us to dashboard a lot of metrics that we collect, some of the stuff for safety, some of the stuff for energy management, some of the stuff for legality checks and so on," said Harlow.
"So a lot of the data that's incoming to us, we can process more quickly using AI for trend monitoring, spotting patterns, basically, which is one of the things it's good at.
"Similarly for the power unit, they use those kinds of tools in the PU [power unit] group for anomaly detection, so a neural net can represent any continuous function you like.

"If you give it enough neurons, you can plot the most complex squiggly line and then compare those squiggly lines with what's coming off the track and you can see when somebody's oil pressure's dropped or whatever."

A neural net is the basic AI structure, which would be big enough to model any pattern - and anomaly detection works by learning what normal traces look like then flagging anything that deviates from that.
This is more useful for informing FIA analysis as the AI tools are good at essentially predicting an outcome for a different event based on interrogating the data fed into it.
Building the model to learn as it goes will also turn the process from one-off rule-making to a continuous loop as the tools learn how any new regulations work in action and keep evolving.

This is useful for big rule changes when previous data does not accurately reflect the new cars although the caveat is that neural nets can be so-called black boxes, where the internal decision-making process is difficult or impossible for humans to trace, so the FIA would need to be able to understand why its tools have flagged something.

And with F1 cars being so complex, AI tools would be weak at making something entirely new for now, although the idea of 'prompt engineering' is something that could materialise further down the line.
"Already there's work started on new aerodynamic concepts for future cars based on the learnings from these [2026] ones," said Harlow. “Some different ideas that we could try and investigate.
"I suppose the generative part of AI is something we could imagine in the future, but at the moment it's human-driven, engineer-driven.
"Prompt engineering your car, that's obviously all about the training and the evolution of the models, and it takes a lot of computing and a lot of money to try and do that stuff for sure.
"I'm sure it'll come."
One area the FIA should be able to gain in with its AWS partnership is accessing the latest GPU (graphics processing unit) hardware.

CFD traditionally ran on CPUs but the software is now being rewritten to run on GPUs, often several times faster and capable of handling huge numbers of simple calculations at once, which suits both AI and CFD. Better hardware means quicker, more accurate results.
Harlow gave the example of the porpoising effect that caught out several teams and the FIA at the start of the ground-effect era in 2022 as something that could potentially benefit from this.
"So instead of having to run just a round, steady-state CFD simulation, you can run a time-sensitive simulation in unsteady conditions," said Harlow.
"And perhaps with a phenomenon like porpoising, get a bit more of an understanding before it's a problem or before it's seen in full size."
Another area AI is likely to feed into the FIA's processes is using large language models that are more fit-for-purpose to support team enquiries into legalities and stress-testing of regulations.

This means making a more private, secure version than ChatGPT or Claude-type AIs to ring-fence intellectual property, so confidential material stays inside the FIA but can be used to check such a vast, complicated rulebook and its interrelated clauses.

The breadth of uses also includes assisting dashboards managing safety, energy management and legality checks at the track, and supporting the enhanced remote operations centre in Geneva that supports race control remotely during events.

This may include assisting with track limits, as the current automated system can throw up hundreds of incidents that a human has to check whereas AI could provide a prioritised list or prompt a series of checks before a judgement is made so humans still decide, but do so faster and more consistently.
